subject: Data lineage & KMS chain-of-custody — Acadia SSQ follow-up
messages:
From: security@acadia.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@acadia.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 08:02:00 -0800
Subject: Data handling lineage + KMS custody request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. Acadia's security team needs a short, focused response to two items from our DPA and SSQ: 1) a concise data lineage showing where PII enters, flows, and is persisted (including ephemeral caches), and 2) a KMS chain-of-custody map listing which team/role holds each key and which cloud region the keys are provisioned from.

Can you confirm whether you can provide a diagram + a simple table we can include in our compliance packet? Our procurement partner (copied) wants to know if anything here requires an additional procurement approval.

Target: we hope to close the security review by next Thursday (2027-12-23).

Thanks,
Jared Malloy
Information Security, Acadia Health
attachments: none
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: security@acadia.com
Cc: procurement@acadia.com, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2027 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data handling lineage + KMS custody request

Jared —

Appreciate the clear ask. We can provide both artifacts: a simplified PII lineage diagram and a KMS custody table. Quick notes on scope so we stay aligned:

- Scope: customer request covers data ingested via our Hosted API and Dedicated deployments. Private on-prem deployments have a separate custodian model (we'll flag differences).
- PII definition: we will follow the SSQ mapping you attached earlier (names, identifiers, contact info, and health-related data). If you have a narrower set, tell us.
- KMS custody: we'll list Redwood roles (e.g., key-admin, infra-sre) and the external services (cloud KMS or HSM) we integrate with; we will not enumerate individual engineers.

Deliverables (proposed):
1) pii_lineage_diagram_v1.svg — flow nodes: API ingress → prefix/KV cache (ephemeral) → inference runtime (KV + model context) → metrics & logs (pseudonymized) → optional persistence (customer-configured store). Diagram will label where PII is transient vs persisted.
2) kms_custody_table_v1.csv — columns: key_id_scope, key_type (customer-managed / service-managed), holder_role, region, retention/rotation cadence, evidence_link.
3) mini-dpia-summary.pdf — 1 page summary highlighting controls and residual risk for Acadia.

Attachments I plan to send shortly: pii_lineage_diagram_v1.svg, kms_custody_table_v1.csv, mini-dpia-summary.pdf. None of this requires procurement approval on our side; the artifacts are informational. If Acadia requires signed attestation beyond the DPA (e.g., KMS escrow or third-party audit report), that may trigger procurement conversations.

Estimate: I'll share the initial artifacts by EOD tomorrow (2027-12-15).

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Privacy Engineering
Redwood Inference
attachments: pii_lineage_diagram_v1.svg (diagram), kms_custody_table_v1.csv (spreadsheet), mini-dpia-summary.pdf (doc)
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: security@acadia.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Data handling lineage + KMS custody request

Jared —

Quick clarifications from our side before we finalize the artifacts:

1) Can you confirm whether Acadia will consider telemetry and anonymized logs as outside PII scope? We will mark metrics as pseudonymized by default, but logs that contain request payloads will be marked as potentially sensitive.

2) For cross-border concerns: do you need per-region key custody (i.e., separate records for EU vs US) or is a single account-level mapping sufficient?

3) If you need a timestamped attestation for your procurement folder, we can add a short signed cover note to the mini-dpia-summary.pdf — will that suffice, or do you require an executed addendum?

I'll fold your responses into the csv fields (region, residency, attestation_required).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: none
